chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: "Saludos Amigos" armed forces broadcast recordings
summary: They recorded forty or fifty shows for the army at La Conga, a studio and the Palladium, with four-hour sessions; he also mentions Muzak.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: In - ahh - after Decca, you did some radio broadcasts for the Armed Forces, 'Saludos Amigos'.
"Saludos Amigos"
Okay, now someone says they have air-
checks of that, I've been trying to get them. Do you remember the "Saludos Amigos" program?
Yes.
Tell me about it. How did it come about and where were they broadcasting from.

Well, it was in -- "Saludos Amigos" was recorded in La Conga and it was recorded in a studio for the army, and then we did few recordings at Palladium Ballroom, in 1947 and we did a few recordings from La Conga, where the Casablanca is now, that was Birdland, we made a recording for the army.
How long would it take to record?
It was like there was no stop, no mistake, whatever happened.....
Right.
....the recording.
No, but do you remember the band recording show for them? Was it an hour that you had to play?
No, more than that.
More?
We was there, let's say, playing four-hour section and everytime that we come back to the band start the record, whatever, we were playing.
They were done on records, there were no tapes at that time.
No.
Okay, did you ever get to hear any of those programs?
No.
You never got to hear them. About how many of them did you did?
Could be a good forty or fifty copies.
Really!! For 'Saludos Amigos'?
Yes.
Forty or fifty shows?
Yes.
WOW!! and did you always do different numbers for the repertoire?
Yes.
Uh - Huh
Well, we already had four or five-hundred numbers.
I see. Okay, there came a time that you recorded for Musak, do you remember when that was?
Yes
About what time period was that?
I think it was in 1946 or '47.
